title: France records 2,025 excess deaths at peak of heatwave as Europe braces for more extreme weather
facts: The Public Health France agency recorded 2,025 excess deaths between 22 June and 28 June.
French health minister Stéphanie Rist reported an increase in deaths among individuals over the age of 45.
France experienced its highest country-wide average temperature on 24 June.
Temperatures reached almost 41 degrees Celsius in Paris on 24 June.
Half of France was placed under a red heat alert during the June heatwave.
The Copernicus climate service reported that Europe is heating up twice as fast as the global average.
Belgium recorded 1,222 excess deaths during the June heatwave.
Almost half of the excess heatwave deaths in Belgium occurred in individuals aged 85 and over.
The death rate in the Paris region increased by 62 percent between 22 June and 28 June.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated that 72 people died by drowning since 18 June.
Dutch authorities reported approximately 480 excess deaths during the heatwave in the Netherlands.
Météo-France issued red alerts for forest fires in the southern part of France.
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu reported nearly 7,000 fires had broken out since the start of the summer season.
Nearly 3,000 people were evacuated following a wildfire in the town of Sainte-Marie-la-Mer.
The government of Portugal declared a state of alert.
